issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is unbounded, risking unbounded memory growth on stalls or crashes.
issues.detail: The list[LogRecord] retained between _on_setup and init_recording/_on_cleanup has no cap. A hang or slow crash under heavy logging grows it without limit. Replace with a bounded deque(maxlen=N) or enforce an explicit invariant in emit().

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer locates the OTLP LoggingHandler by scanning root logger handlers instead of holding a reference.
issues.detail: JobContext reaches into logging.getLogger().handlers searching for an OTLP LoggingHandler, leaking telemetry internals across the module boundary and silently no-oping if not found. _setup_cloud_tracer knows which handler it installed; store and pass it. This is the very upload path the PR claims to fix.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry mutates global root logger state by removing every LoggingHandler instance.
issues.detail: The function now strips all opentelemetry LoggingHandler instances from the root logger, including any a user installed independently. The frame is unstated and the side effect is global. Scope removal to the handler this module installed by keeping a reference at setup time.

issues.description: init_recording is overloaded to also tear down the early-log buffering handler on its early-return paths.
issues.detail: The contract previously had clean preconditions (not initialized, cloud URL) and one postcondition. It now silently performs buffering teardown for unrelated callers, including a synthetic call from _on_cleanup with audio/traces/transcript all false. Split into init_recording plus an explicit _ensure_crash_log_pipeline or teardown call.

issues.description: Lifecycle methods on JobContext should collapse into a single LogBuffer object that owns its handler.
issues.detail: _start_log_buffering, _stop_log_buffering, _flush_early_log_buffer, and the _on_cleanup branch all manage one handler with a None-dance on _early_log_handler. A small LogBuffer with attach/detach/replay removes the scattered state and makes the invariants visible.

issues.description: Unrelated changes (pytest-xdist removal, test_plugin_google_stt skip, worker.py race fix reorder) bundled without justification.
issues.detail: The makefile drops -n auto and excludes a plugin test; worker.py reorders pending-assignment registration before _queue_msg to close a real race. None are motivated by the PR description. Split or annotate so each change can be reviewed against its own contract and reverted independently.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes a real defect — crash logs never reaching the server — but accretes complexity in the logging subsystem with leaky abstractions and unstated invariants. The unanimous P1s: _BufferingHandler is unbounded, _flush_early_log_buffer finds its OTLP sink by scanning root handlers instead of holding a reference, and _shutdown_telemetry mutates global root logger state. init_recording has also been overloaded to serve unrelated teardown callers. Tighten the telemetry module's contract (own the handler, bound the buffer, expose replay as a first-class operation) and split out the unrelated test/build/worker changes.
